title: Select and Update the DOM
summary: Connect JavaScript to the page by selecting elements, changing text, and creating new elements safely.

sketchBlocks.title: querySelector finds an element; textContent changes what it says
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
The **DOM** is JavaScript's object representation of the page. Before JavaScript can change an element, it needs a reference to that element.

```js
const status = document.querySelector("#event-status");
status.textContent = "Registration is open";
```

Line by line:

1. `document.querySelector("#event-status")` finds the first matching element.
2. The result is stored in `status`.
3. `status.textContent = ...` replaces the element's text.

Keep selection and update as separate visible steps while learning. That makes it easier to tell whether a bug came from **finding the element** or **changing the element**.

quizDraft.title: Update a reading goal
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: A reading-goal page has an existing status element, but its message is outdated. Task: Select `#reading-goal` and change its text to `"Read 20 pages today"`. Expected result: the Preview shows the new reading goal in the existing element.
quizDraft.hint: Select first, then update the selected element.

help.concept: DOM code needs an element reference before it can change that element.
help.hint_1: Use the id selector for reading-goal.
help.hint_2: Assign the new sentence to the element's text property.

quizDraft.solutionCode:
const goal = document.querySelector("#reading-goal");
goal.textContent = "Read 20 pages today";
